definitions.explanation: A commercial entertainment facility with coin-operated video games, crane games, purikura (photo booths), and other amusement machines.

examples.japanese: ゲームセンター⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦{帰|かえ}り→帰り：01275_kaeri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ゲームセンター⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{寄|よ}った→寄る：02440_yoru⟧。
examples.english: I stopped by the arcade on the way home from school.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ゲームセンター⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦クレーンゲーム→クレーンゲーム：17040_kureengeemu⟧やプリクラ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{家族連|かぞくづ}れ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: At modern arcades, crane games and photo booths are popular, and many families visit too.

notes:
A Japanese-English compound (wasei eigo) from "game" + "center." Almost always abbreviated as ⟦ゲーセン→ゲーセン：07329_geesen⟧ in casual speech. A major part of Japanese entertainment culture, particularly popular among teenagers and young adults.

FORMS:
⟦ゲーセン→ゲーセン：07329_geesen⟧ is the standard casual abbreviation. The full form ゲームセンター is used in formal contexts, signs, and written Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ゲームセンター⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go to an arcade
- ゲームセンター⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧: to play at an arcade
- ゲームセンター⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{景品|けいひん}→景品：08319_keihin⟧: arcade prizes
- ゲームセンター{通|がよ}い: being a regular at the arcade

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese arcades are distinct from Western arcades in several ways. They typically occupy multiple floors and are organized by game type: fighting games, rhythm games, crane games (UFOキャッチャー), medal games, and purikura (プリクラ). While the global arcade industry has largely declined, Japanese game centers remain culturally significant, though they too have been decreasing in number.
